title: The Brain Paradox: Expected Sweet Juice Fires Zero Extra Spikes
description:
Behavioral & Circuit Analysis — Wolfram Schultz, Dayan & Montague (1997): Dopamine Is NOT 'Pleasure' — It's Exact 'Actual Minus Expected' Surprise Math!, grounded in Wolfram Schultz, Peter Dayan, P. Read Montague (1997) (Science). Empirical findings show that ask ten people on the street 'What is dopamine?' and nine will say 'The brain's pleasure molecule!' — yet in *March 1997 (Science, SRC1), Wolfram Schultz, Peter Dayan, and Read Montague published one 3-row neural raster plot* that demolished the 'dopamine = pleasure' myth forever.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how ventral tegmental area, nucleus accumbens, prefrontal cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that in Row 1 — Unexpected Reward (No Cue + Drop of Sweet Fruit Juice): a drop of apple juice arrives out of nowhere with zero warning — and midbrain ventral tegmental area (VTA) / substantia nigra dopamine neurons fire a sharp +BURST right when the juice hits the tongue.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Wolfram Schultz, Peter Dayan, P. Read Montague (1997). A Neural Substrate of Prediction and Reward. Science. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.275.5306.1593
- Wolfram Schultz (2024). The Dopamine Reward Prediction Error Signal. https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4816666
- Wolfram Schultz (1997). Reward responses of dopamine neurons: A biological reinforcement signal. Lecture Notes in Computer Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/bfb0020125
